### TL;DR  
Yes – the **Mapbox GL Style Spec** validator (available as a CLI via npm) will tell you whether a style JSON conforms to the spec that MapLibre GL JS follows.  

```bash
# Install the validator globally (one‑time)
npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec   # or @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

# Run it against your exported style
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate path/to/style.json
# (or `maplibre-gl-style-spec validate …` if you installed that package)
```

If the command exits with `0` you’re good to go; any non‑zero exit code is accompanied by a list of validation errors/warnings that you can fix before deploying.

---

## Why this works

* **MapLibre GL JS** is a fork of **Mapbox GL JS v1** and deliberately keeps the same style‑spec version (the “v8” spec).  
* The official `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec` package ships a full JSON‑Schema validator plus a tiny CLI wrapper that checks a style file against that schema.  
* MapLibre maintains a thin wrapper package (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`) that simply re‑exports the same validator, so you can use either name.

Both packages validate **everything** that the spec defines:

| Category | What gets checked |
|----------|-------------------|
| **Core spec** | required top‑level keys (`version`, `sources`, `layers`), correct data types, allowed values for `type`, `layout`, `paint`, etc. |
| **Source definitions** | valid source types (`vector`, `raster`, `geojson`, `image`, `video`), required fields (`url`, `tiles`, `data`), proper URL syntax. |
| **Layer definitions** | correct `source-layer` names, valid `filter` expressions, supported `layout`/`paint` properties for the layer type. |
| **Expressions** | proper syntax, correct number of arguments, type‑checking of literals. |
| **Deprecated / unsupported keys** | flags usage of Mapbox‑only extensions (e.g., `mapbox://` URLs, `glyphs` that require a Mapbox token, `metadata.mapbox:...`). |
| **Version** | ensures `version` is `8` (the only version MapLibre understands). |

If the validator finds a Mapbox‑only feature (like a `mapbox://fonts/...` URL) it will **error** because MapLibre cannot resolve those resources without a Mapbox token. Those are the exact things you want to catch before you ship.

---

## Installing & Using the CLI

### 1. Install (global or project‑local)

```bash
# Global install – handy for ad‑hoc checks
npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec

# OR, if you prefer the MapLibre‑scoped package
npm i -g @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
```

> **Tip:** If you’re already using a Node‑based CI pipeline, you can add the package as a dev‑dependency instead of a global install:

```bash
npm i -D @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec   # then run via npx
npx mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json
```

### 2. Run the validator

```bash
# Basic usage – prints errors to stdout, exits 0 on success
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate ./my-style.json
```

#### Common flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--quiet` | Suppress the “✔︎ valid” message; only prints errors. |
| `--verbose` | Show every validation step (useful for debugging complex styles). |
| `--schema` | Output the JSON‑Schema that the validator uses (for custom tooling). |
| `--format json` | Emit errors as JSON (good for CI parsers). |

Example for CI:

```bash
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json --format json > style-validation.json
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  cat style-validation.json
  exit 1
fi
```

---

## What the validator **won’t** catch (and how to handle it)

| Issue | Why the validator misses it | How to address it |
|-------|----------------------------|-------------------|
| **Network‑level problems** (e.g., a tile URL that returns 404) | Validation is static – it only checks syntax, not runtime fetchability. | Run a quick “smoke test” with `curl`/`wget` or spin up a local MapLibre GL JS preview (Maputnik, `maplibre-gl-js` demo page). |
| **Custom extensions** (e.g., `metadata.myCompany:foo`) | The spec allows arbitrary `metadata`, but MapLibre may ignore unknown keys. | Keep custom metadata under a namespaced key that you know your own code reads; the validator will ignore it. |
| **Performance‑related settings** (e.g., huge `maxzoom` ranges) | Not part of the spec. | Review the style manually or use MapLibre’s `debug` mode to spot over‑zoomed tiles. |
| **Unsupported Mapbox‑only layers** (e.g., `fill-extrusion` with `fill-extrusion-pattern` that references a Mapbox sprite) | The validator flags the missing sprite URL, but it can’t know whether you’ve replaced the sprite with a self‑hosted one. | Ensure any `sprite` or `glyphs` URLs point to assets you control (e.g., `https://my.cdn.com/sprite`). |

---

## Quick “cheat‑sheet” of the most common Mapbox‑to‑MapLibre gotchas

| Mapbox‑only feature | What the validator reports | Fix |
|---------------------|----------------------------|-----|
| `glyphs: "mapbox://fonts/{username}/{fontstack}"` | **Error:** `glyphs` URL must be an HTTP(S) URL. | Host your own glyphs (e.g., `https://my.cdn.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`) or use the open‑source **glyphs** server from the MapLibre community. |
| `sprite: "mapbox://sprites/{username}/{style}"` | **Error:** `sprite` URL must be an HTTP(S) URL. | Publish the sprite sheet to a static host and reference it with a full URL. |
| `source: { type: "vector", url: "mapbox://..." }` | **Error:** `url` must be a valid TileJSON URL. | Convert the Mapbox Tileset URL to a TileJSON endpoint you host (or use the `tiles` array directly). |
| `metadata.mapbox:...` | **Warning** (if you use the `--strict` flag) | Remove or rename the key; MapLibre ignores it anyway. |
| `filter` expressions using `["has", "mapbox:..."]` | **Error** if the property name contains a colon (colon is allowed, but MapLibre may not expose that property). | Rename the property in your source data or adjust the filter. |
| `text-font` referencing a Mapbox‑only font stack | **Error** if the font stack isn’t available in your glyphs. | Update `text-font` to match the fonts you actually serve. |

---

## Integrating into a CI pipeline (example with GitHub Actions)

```yaml
name: Validate MapLibre style

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  style-validation:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install validator
        run: npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec

      - name: Validate style.json
        id: validate
        run: |
          mapbox-gl-style-spec validate ./styles/style.json --format json > validation.json
          echo "validation=$(cat validation.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        continue-on-error: true   # we want to capture the exit code ourselves

      - name: Fail if invalid
        if: steps.validate.outcome != 'success'
        run: |
          echo "❌ Style validation failed"
          cat validation.json
          exit 1
```

The job will **fail** the PR if any validation error appears, giving you a safety net before the style ever reaches production.

---

## Alternative / Complementary tools

| Tool | What it does | When you might use it |
|------|--------------|-----------------------|
| **Maputnik** (`npm i -g maputnik`) | Web UI editor that loads a style and instantly shows validation errors in the UI. Great for interactive debugging. | When you want a visual “lint” alongside the CLI. |
| **mapbox-gl-native style validator** (`npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-native`) | Older validator used by the native SDKs; still works for v8 styles. | Legacy pipelines that already depend on the native validator. |
| **stylelint‑style‑spec** (community plugin) | Lints style JSON as part of a broader `stylelint` run (e.g., alongside CSS). | If you already run `stylelint` for other assets and want a single command. |
| **Custom Node script** (`require('@mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec').validate(style)`) | Gives you programmatic access to the validation results (e.g., to generate a custom report). | When you need more than just “pass/fail” (e.g., counting warnings, auto‑fix suggestions). |

---

## Full example: From Mapbox Studio export to a production‑ready MapLibre style

```bash
# 1️⃣ Export from Mapbox Studio → style.json
# 2️⃣ Replace Mapbox‑only URLs (glyphs, sprite, source URLs) with self‑hosted equivalents.
# 3️⃣ Run the validator
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json
#    → If you see errors about `glyphs` or `sprite`, fix them now.
# 4️⃣ (Optional) Spin up Maputnik to double‑check visual rendering
maputnik style.json &
# 5️⃣ Commit & push – CI will re‑run the validator automatically.
```

If the validator prints **“✔︎ style.json is valid”** (or exits with code 0), you can be confident that the JSON conforms to the spec that MapLibre GL JS expects, and you’re ready to deploy.

---

### TL;DR Recap

| Step | Command |
|------|---------|
| Install validator | `npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec` (or `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`) |
